readme: AUTHORITATIVE CONTRACT for any AI agent (Claude, ChatGPT, Codex, ...) that publishes study content for the IELTS practice web app. Human-readable specs live in specs/ — start at specs/README.md or AGENTS.md. This JSON file is the machine-readable platform summary. Sibling files lesson-template.json (schema 1) and dynamic-template.json (schema 2) show annotated examples. v5: contentUpdatedAt records the last meaningful content edit so the app can skip unchanged files efficiently.

publishing.layout: One folder per source under the content root: claude-cowork/, chatgpt/, codex/, <your-agent-name>/. Inside your folder organize freely (e.g. lessons/, news/, speaking/, quizzes/). The 'source' field in your JSON (or your folder name) is the source label shown in the app.

write.method: Local agents write files directly into the content root and run convert_lessons.py from the tool folder to refresh manifest.json, then push to GitHub. Remote agents (e.g. ChatGPT) commit their .json via the GitHub connector to main; the repository owner's hourly pipeline pulls, re-indexes the manifest, and publishes.
rules: ADD or UPDATE only — never delete
never overwrite files you did not create
never touch other sources' folders, templates/, ipa/, index.html, manifest.json, or the app files
any cadence: several files per hour, daily, weekly, adhoc
filename stems must be unique across ALL sources (use an agent marker like -gpt- in the stem)

publishing.read: Public reads (templates, state, existing content) use GitHub Pages: https://mtm0101.github.io/public-sites/claude-cowork/ielts-hourly-practice-tool/<path-under-tool-folder>?t=<timestamp>. Example: .../data/templates/template-spec.json. Pages lags commits by a minute or two.
publishing.discovery: The app loads content ONLY from manifest.json next to index.html, rebuilt by convert_lessons.py on the owner's machine each run (it indexes every study .json under the content root by SHAPE: sections[] = study item; items[] with questions = speaking set; templates/ipa/state files are skipped). A committed file appears in the app after the owner's next pipeline run.
publishing.userData: The S3 bucket (https://t-do-not-delete-ihp-7xf29m4kq9vnb1zt8we5yu3hj6kf0fd4jh1sa9vr2mn.s3.amazonaws.com) stores exactly one object: user-data.json — the app's own progress sync. NO agent may ever read, write, or overwrite it.

fileNaming: Free-form, but must end .json and the filename stem (without .json) must be UNIQUE across ALL sources — it becomes the item id when 'id' is omitted. Recommended: <type>-YYYY-MM-DD-HHMM-<slug>.json, e.g. ielts-2026-07-09-1500-topic05-education.json or news-2026-07-10-daily-headlines.json.

studyItem.description: Any lesson, news article, quiz, test, reading/listening set, email exercise, etc. Schema 1 (full IELTS lesson) and schema 2 (generic) share this shape; only conventions differ.

required.sections: array of section objects (min 1) — see 'section' below. THIS is what makes a file a study item.

stronglyRecommended.id: string, unique; defaults to filename stem
stronglyRecommended.title: string, display title (English), short, no dates
stronglyRecommended.type: free label: lesson | news | quiz | test | listening | reading | writing | email | ... (shown as chip + filter)
stronglyRecommended.source: free label: claude-cowork | chatgpt | codex | ...; defaults to your bucket folder name
stronglyRecommended.category: free grouping label, e.g. ielts-hourly, daily-news, worldcup
stronglyRecommended.dateTime: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM local; defaults to the S3 upload time
stronglyRecommended.contentUpdatedAt: ISO 8601 timestamp with timezone for the last meaningful content edit. Set it when creating the file and advance it whenever content changes; never advance it for reads, downloads, manifest rebuilds, formatting-only no-ops, or unchanged republishes.
stronglyRecommended.words: array of plain-text vocabulary headwords (used by search); [] if none

section.id: string, unique within the item, [a-zA-Z0-9_-] only (e.g. vocab, reading, s1, s1-1)
section.title: string, human heading (the app renders it — do NOT repeat it inside html)
section.level: 1 (default), 2 or 3 — level>1 renders as an indented sub-section; every level gets its own nav link, confidence buttons and bookmark
section.html: string of section body HTML following htmlConventions below

studyItem.fullIeltsLessonConvention: exactly 6 sections with ids in order: vocab, reading, listening, writing, speaking, strategy — titles: Vocabulary / Reading / Listening / Writing (Task 2) / Speaking / Strategy Note. See lesson-template.json.

speakingSource.description: Speaking Q&A practice sets (rendered in the app's dedicated Speaking section with per-question confidence rating).

items.topic: short topic name shown in lists
items.title: longer title

htmlConventions.bilingualRule:
THE core rule: every English sentence goes in its own

…

, IMMEDIATELY followed by its Vietnamese translation in its own

…

. ONE sentence per .en element — never merge a paragraph into one element, never mix EN and VN in the same element. The app attaches per-sentence flagging, audio and word tap-to-pronounce to each .en. A missing .vn line is a defect.
forbiddenContent: the section's own <h2> (the app renders section headers)
literal marker words anywhere: 'Meaning:', 'Definition:', 'Example:', 'Nghĩa:', 'Ý nghĩa:', 'Ví dụ:', 'VD:' — the app colour-codes definition vs example lines automatically by position
htmlConventions.headings: use <h3> and <h4> for sub-headings inside a section; bold with <strong>
htmlConventions.ipa: US (General American) IPA in slashes inside class="ipa" elements; IPA lines are the only untranslated lines
htmlConventions.vocabCard:
headword /IPA/

VN of headword

simple English definition

/IPA of definition/

VN of definition

example sentence

/IPA of example/

VN of example

— exactly one div.head per card (it powers the app's word-flag star and UK/US pronunciation buttons); first p.en in a card = definition (teal), later p.en = examples (violet)

htmlConventions.sectionsHtmlRequired: Every section MUST include a non-empty html string. The app does NOT render raw stories[], items[], or {en,vi} objects — only sections[].html. Section title must be a plain string, not {en,vi}.
